:::{#thm-pd-operations}
#### Operations that preserve definiteness

1. If $\matr{C}$ is a $p \times p$ positive definite matrix (@def-positive-definite)
   and $\matr{A}$ is a $p \times k$ matrix with $k$ linearly independent columns,
   then the $k \times k$ matrix $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{C} \matr{A}$ is positive definite.
2. If $\matr{A}_1$ and $\matr{A}_2$ are positive definite $p \times p$ matrices
   and $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 > 0$,
   then $\alpha_1 \matr{A}_1 + \alpha_2 \matr{A}_2$ is positive definite.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
$\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{C} \matr{A}$ is symmetric:
$\tp{(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{C} \matr{A})} = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{\matr{C}}\,\tp{(\tp{\matr{A}})} = \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{C} \matr{A}$
(@thm-transpose-product, twice; $\matr{C}$ symmetric; @def-matrix-transpose).
For $\vx \ne \vzero_k$, $\matr{A} \vx \ne \vzero_p$,
since the columns of $\matr{A}$ are independent (@thm-matvec-columns, @def-linearly-independent), and

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx}\,(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{C} \matr{A})\,\vx
&= \tp{(\matr{A} \vx)}\,\matr{C}\,(\matr{A} \vx)
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product, @thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&> 0.
&& \text{(} \matr{C} \text{ positive definite, } \matr{A} \vx \ne \vzero \text{)}
\ea
$$

**Part 2.**
$\alpha_1 \matr{A}_1 + \alpha_2 \matr{A}_2$ is symmetric:
its transpose is $\alpha_1 \tp{\matr{A}_1} + \alpha_2 \tp{\matr{A}_2} = \alpha_1 \matr{A}_1 + \alpha_2 \matr{A}_2$
(@thm-transpose-sum, @def-scalar-mult, @def-matrix-transpose).
For $\vx \ne \vzero$,

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx}\,(\alpha_1 \matr{A}_1 + \alpha_2 \matr{A}_2)\,\vx
&= \tp{\vx}\,(\alpha_1 \matr{A}_1)\,\vx + \tp{\vx}\,(\alpha_2 \matr{A}_2)\,\vx
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib, twice)}
\\
&= \alpha_1\,\tp{\vx} \matr{A}_1 \vx + \alpha_2\,\tp{\vx} \matr{A}_2 \vx
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\\
&> 0.
&& \text{(each term is positive)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-pd-operations}
#### Building positive definite matrices

- With $\matr{C} = \matr{I}_3$ and $\mX$ of @exm-pd-gram,
  part 1 gives again that $\tp{\mX} \mX$ is positive definite.
- With $\alpha_1 = 2$, $\matr{A}_1 = \matr{I}_2$ (@exm-positive-definite), $\alpha_2 = 1$
  and $\matr{A}_2 = \tp{\mX} \mX = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ 6 & 14 \end{bmatrix}$ (@exm-pd-gram),
  part 2 gives that $2 \matr{I}_2 + \tp{\mX} \mX = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 6 & 16 \end{bmatrix}$ is positive definite.
- An aside beyond part 2:
  $\matr{I}_2 + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
  is positive definite plus positive semidefinite;
  its quadratic form is $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + (x_1 + x_2)^2 > 0$ for $\vx \ne \vzero$,
  so it is positive definite, in line with its eigenvalues $3$ and $1$ (@exm-eigenvalue).
- Independence is needed in part 1:
  with $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, whose columns are equal,
  $\tp{\matr{A}}\,\matr{I}_2\,\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$,
  and $(1, -1)$ gives quadratic form $0$.

:::
